approach: In `producer_loop` (producer.rs), after the work-tree checks for a pass, run the configured checks on the producer's tree with the existing `run_check`. Skip a nested run, a pinned run and a pass with no change. The new `Athena::loop_check_failures` in run/checks.rs does it. It builds a `SnapExec` with `snapshot` = the producer's snapshot, `prepared` = `snapshot.work_tree_tree()`, the Verify-side env, and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` pointing at a temporary index filled by `git add -A`, so `git ls-files` lists new files. It routes with `routing::route` and runs each non-skipped spec through `Exec::exec`, stopping at the first failure. A failure that is not timed out and not pre-existing on the baseline (`verify::is_pre_existing`) becomes a `CheckFailure` (name, command, exit status, output tail). Each failure adds one short problem string to `problems` and `report_problems`. The string names the check, the command and the exit status, so the stored invocation detail ("self-check failed: …") names it. The full command and output tail go into the brief through a new `append_check_failures` in send_back.rs, chained in the same way as `append_mirror_drift` and `append_missing_changelog`. The existing single send-back (`PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1`) carries it. At the limit the problem sits in `report_problems`, so it is printed and stored as `report_gaps`, and the verifier is told. The verifier still runs its own checks. `SnapExec` gains one field so the in-loop run skips the test-only `check_seam` and starts with `gated = true`. That leaves every existing seam-driven test and every disk-gate test unchanged. A new brief section and one net-zero line in producer.md tell the producer. D182 records it.

decisions.choice: Reuse `SnapExec` for the in-loop run, with `prepared` = the producer tree just taken, `gated = true` and a new `fakeable: bool` field set false for it (true in mod.rs:2037).
decisions.reason: `SnapExec::exec` (run/checks.rs:98-145) already gives the check slot queue, the warm target link, `run_check`, the kill switch and a `restore_to(prepared)` that removes check-made files from the producer tree. The in-loop run is therefore the same as the verification run. `gated = true` leaves the disk gate to verification, so `low_once_verifying` style tests keep their call order. `fakeable = false` makes the in-loop run skip `check_seam` (checks.rs:116-119), so the many existing tests that install a seam still see one check call per check, and the new tests use real `sh -c` checks.

rejected.option: Call `run_check` directly with a hand-built `CheckContext` (as `format_stage` does, producer.rs:196)
rejected.why: It bypasses build slots and the warm target link, so the in-loop `cargo test` would build cold in the producer's own target dir. It also leaves check-made files in the tree that `change_list` then sees.

rejected.option: Leave `SnapExec::exec` as it is and let the seam answer the in-loop run
rejected.why: Every seam-driven test (tests.rs:4521, 4959, 5023, 5252, 5590, 6390, 6788) would get an extra check call. Failing fakes would add send-backs and change the producer counts.

decisions.choice: Render the failure with a new `append_check_failures(text, &[CheckFailure])` in send_back.rs, chained after `append_mirror_drift` and `append_missing_changelog` (producer.rs:639). Do not add a seventh parameter to `send_back_text_scoped`.
decisions.reason: Later send-back additions already use this shape (send_back.rs:219-267). It adds one leading sentence after `## Sent back` (the intro speaks only of criteria) and a section after the lists. It leaves the four `send_back_text*` wrappers and their many test callers unchanged.

rejected.option: Add a `checks: &[CheckFailure]` parameter to `send_back_text_scoped` and its wrappers
rejected.why: It touches every wrapper and call site (producer.rs:622-638, send_back.rs tests) for no gain over the append pattern.

decisions.choice: Only a real, new failure is sent back: not timed out (`checks::timed_out`), not pre-existing on the baseline (`verify::is_pre_existing(run, closing.baseline.as_ref())`). `LowDisk` and `SlotWait` from the in-loop run become a `checks     not run before the verifier: …` UI line. The kill-switch error propagates.
decisions.reason: Verification already holds a job whose only failures timed out (`held_for_timeout`) and excludes pre-existing failures from the verdict. Sending the producer back for either would have it chase a fault it cannot fix. A disk or slot wait is judged at verification, which holds the job there.

rejected.why: It spends the one send-back on a timeout or on a base failure the verdict already ignores.

decisions.choice: Run the in-loop checks on every pass, including the second, and put the failure summary in both `problems` and `report_problems`. Skip a nested run, a pinned run (`ctx.pin_dir`, as `format_stage` does) and a pass with an empty change list.
decisions.reason: A check still failing after the send-back must reach the verifier as flagged (criterion 2). `report_problems` becomes `report_gaps`, which candidate.rs:47-50 and verification.rs:100-108 already carry to the verifier. An empty change list fails as an idle producer after the loop.

rejected.option: Run only on the first pass
rejected.why: Nothing would flag a still-failing check, and a producer that breaks a check while fixing another would not be caught.

decisions.choice: Do not edit decision-links.toml. D182 is worded without the words amends, supersedes or superseded, so the log parse finds no hit that needs a `[[link]]`. It says D115 and D156 stand.
decisions.reason: The only `[[governs]]` entry is D08 (candidate.rs and snapshot.rs), and neither file is touched. The change amends no earlier decision. Criterion 7 asks for a link only when one is needed.

rejected.why: D115 (recorded checks on the same tree count as evidence) is applied, not revised.

risks.mitigation: Cost: each pass of a job now runs fmt, clippy and the full test on the producer's tree, and the same checks run again at verification. The in-loop run stops at the first failing check. It takes slots through `SnapExec`, so it waits like any check. It shares the warm slot target, so third-party crates stay compiled, and the workspace crates are rebuilt at verification (checks.rs:233-239). The producer's own target dir is untouched. The run is skipped for a nested run, a pinned run and an empty change list. Not measured: the added wall time per job. The producer states this in D182's Tradeoff, and it is not fixed by this plan.

risks.risk: The producer fixes only the first failing check.
risks.mitigation: The in-loop run reports only the first failing check, because `run_local`-style stopping hides later ones. The brief says later checks may also fail, and the verifier still runs all of them. Do not lift the stop here.

risks.risk: Tests outside the deliverables break from the extra producer pass.
risks.mitigation: Existing athena-core tests with `FAILS_ON_EDIT`, and the athena-cli tests that delete README.md, now see a second producer call. The producer runs the full `cargo test -p athena-core` and `cargo test -p athena-cli` and edits only an assertion that counts producers or orders reports. introspection.rs, steward.rs and code_health_hooks.rs are not deliverables. If one of them needs an edit, the producer reports it in open_issues and does not edit it. The scope check would send such an edit back.

risks.risk: A check that writes into the tree changes the candidate.
risks.mitigation: `SnapExec::exec` calls `restore_to(prepared)` after each check with `prepared` taken just before the run, so files a check writes to the tree are removed before the next check and before the change list is taken again. The new test of criterion 4 shows the tree and the change list are as the producer left them (the producer count stays 1).

risks.risk: The temporary index leaks into the verification-time run, or the real index is changed.
risks.mitigation: `git add -A` into a temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE` outside the work tree, as `Snapshot::work_tree_tree` does (athena-git/src/snapshot.rs:209-218). It touches neither the snapshot's real index nor the work tree. `run_check` clears the env, so the variable is set in the env map handed to `CheckContext`. The `TempPath` is held until the checks end. Because `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is in the in-loop env only, the verification-time env is unchanged.

risks.risk: The `ls-files` test could pass in the loop and fail at verification for the same file.
risks.mitigation: The verifier snapshot's own index may not list a candidate-added file for `git ls-files`. That is existing verification behavior and outside this change. The criterion 4 test therefore asserts only the in-loop result (producer count 1) and not the landing.

demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go` (producer_loop). Fixture: `athena_with` with `NEEDS_FIXED_FILE` and `counting(counts, None)` via `editing`. `Counts::all()` gives the producer and verifier counts (tests.rs:2984). The seam exists today.

demonstrations.method: Test `a_failing_check_is_sent_back_before_the_verifier_and_the_fix_reaches_it`. It builds `repo()`, `athena_with(.., NEEDS_FIXED_FILE, ..)` and a script that records every producer prompt and adds FIXED.txt on a send-back. It runs `athena.ask("describe the demo")` then `athena.go(job, AcceptedBy::User, &ui)`. It asserts: state Landed; producer count 2 and verifier count 1; `prompts[0]` has no `## Sent back`; `prompts[1]` has `## Sent back`, the command text `sh -c test -f FIXED.txt || { echo MISSING-FIXED-TXT; exit 1; }` and the output tail `MISSING-FIXED-TXT`; and a UI line `producer   sent back: check probe failed`.
demonstrations.observes: The second producer call's brief names the failed command and its tail. After the fix the verifier runs once and the job lands.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree no send-back happens: the producer count is 1 (the check fails only at verification, so the job is Rejected) and `prompts[1]` is an index panic. The test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go` (producer.rs:272, via run/mod.rs). Fake: the producer script of `FakeAgentDriver`, injected through `athena_with`. It only edits files and returns the report. It does not run the checks, which are the real `run_check` on a real `sh` process. The check command is configuration, not logic under test. The seam exists today (tests.rs:191, 3066). Step 9 adds the const and the wrapper script.

demonstrations.method: First test: `athena_with(.., PASSES, ..)` with `editing(counts, prompts, vec![])`. It asserts producer count 1, verifier count 1, a single prompt with no `## Sent back`, and no UI line starting `producer   sent back`. Second test: the check is a new const `LISTS_NEW_FILE = &["sh","-c","git ls-files --error-unmatch NEW.txt"]`, and the producer adds `NEW.txt` through the `extra` edits of `editing`. It asserts producer count 1 and exactly one prompt, so no send-back happened. It does not assert the final landing, because the verifier-time snapshot is outside this criterion.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core all_checks_passing_means_one_producer_call; cargo test -p athena-core a_file_the_producer_added_is_seen_by_the_in_loop_check
demonstrations.observes: With passing checks there is exactly one producer call and no send-back. A producer-added file is listed by `git ls-files` inside the in-loop check.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the in-loop run always sent back, the first test would see producer count 2. If `GIT_INDEX_FILE` were not set, `git ls-files --error-unmatch NEW.txt` in the snapshot's own index would fail for a file the producer added, so the second test would send back and see producer count 2.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go`. Fixture: `athena_with`, `editing`, `Counts`. The seam exists today. Step 9 adds `LISTS_NEW_FILE` and the two tests.

demonstrations.method: Run the whole `cargo test -p athena-cli` on the final tree. The cli fixtures delete README.md and the `test` check (`test -f README.md && …`, crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:62) fails in the loop, so the producer is sent back once. The fake producer deletes the missing file again (athena-agent/src/fake.rs:107-109 ignores a missing file), so the second pass fails the same check and the verifier still gets the flagged gap and rejects. The producer fixes any assertion on producer counts or order that breaks (lifecycle.rs:1441-1644, 656-664; retry.rs:184, 471, 1378), without weakening it. The listed deliverables lifecycle.rs and retry.rs may be edited for this.
demonstrations.observes: All athena-cli tests pass, including those that delete README.md and expect Rejected (lifecycle.rs:588 and 869-883, retry.rs, introspection.rs, steward.rs, code_health_hooks.rs).
demonstrations.fails_without: If the in-loop run broke the cli fixtures, a test asserting `Rejected` after a README deletion would fail on a changed producer count, report order or retry brief.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `Athena::go` through the cli `Fixture` with `test_config()` and the scenario scripts. They exist today and are only run, not changed, except where an assertion needs the extra producer call.

demonstrations.method: New test in briefs.rs, modelled on `producer_briefs_tell_the_producer_to_run_the_mirror_check` (briefs.rs:2293). It builds a `producer_brief` and asserts the new `## Checks before the verifier` section: it says Athena runs the configured checks before the verifier, that a failure is sent back once with its command and output tail, and that one still failing is flagged to the verifier. It also asserts the section sits after `## Planned files left unchanged` and before `## Report`. The producer edits producer.md line 9 to the exact final text in step 10 and shows with `wc -c` that the file is still 1102 bytes. `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` keeps 1043 of 1200 for the producer set.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-context producer_briefs_say_athena_runs_the_checks_before_the_verifier; cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets; git diff --stat -- crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md
demonstrations.observes: The brief test passes. The budgets tests pass with `budget producer: 1043 of 1200` unchanged. The producer.md byte count is unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no new section or prompt line, the brief test fails on the missing text. A producer.md that changed size would fail `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` and the producer budget test.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `producer_brief` (briefs.rs:675) and the budget tests. No fake is needed. Step 8 adds the section.
